videos.title: AWS Sagemaker AI Crash Course-Customize and Deploy Any LLM
videos.description:
This video provides a complete end-to-end tutorial on fine-tuning, aligning, and deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) serverlessly using Amazon SageMaker AI. Here we demonstrates four levels of LLM customization—Prompt Engineering, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with LoRA, Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), and Reinforcement Learning (RLVR & RLAIF). Using real-world hands-on demonstrations, a base model is customized on legal contracts (Contract NLI dataset), evaluated against expert benchmarks, and served via an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint. Finally, the video covers model alignment using DPO, advanced reinforcement learning notebooks, and low-code customization workflows using an AI agent (Kiru CLI) and the SageMaker Studio UI.

Workshop Link: fandf.co/4gOfvHD

Code github: https://github.com/sourangshupal/sagemaker-model-customization-demo

In today’s episode, we sit down with Barbara Butcher, a retired death investigator from the NYC Office of Chief Medical Examiner who investigated over 5,500 deaths, including homicides, suicides, accidents and disasters, across two decades.

We talk about what Barbara looks for in the first moments at a death scene, why nobody can tell the exact time of death, and what happens to the body after we die. She shares how she reads gunshot wounds, blood spatter, and ligature marks, and how killers stage murders to look like suicides.

We also talk about the real reasons people kill, why so many murders in America go unsolved, and the booby-trapped suicide scene that almost cost her life. She reveals the emotional weight of working through the aftermath of 9/11, the personal toll of shutting down her feelings, and what the dead teach us about living with gratitude.

videos.title: Cardi B on the Moment She Knew Her Marriage Was Over
videos.description:
At five years old, Cardi B sat alone in the school cafeteria with her head down.
Her little sister felt sorry for her.
She wasn't lonely. She was planning her whole life.
Almost everything she planned came true.
So why does it still not feel safe?

In this clip, Cardi B and Jay Shetty talk about growing up in the Bronx. She shares the day a welfare worker talked down to her mom. That moment made her promise she would never raise her kids in the hood.

Cardi opens up about the deepest depression of her life, which stopped her album and everything else. She also shares how she used her party-hosting money to make record labels take her seriously.

Learn why she says your heart, not your head, decides when you're done with someone and the one thing that shows her a man really loves her.
